books.title: Reclaiming Masculinity
books.author: Matt Fuller
books.notes:
i bought this book at a Christian book fair last year while i was doing some soul-searching, but only found the time to read it early this year.

NGL, when i first picked it up, i had plenty of questions about what it means to be a Christian man, and how religion and faith shape our understanding of masculinity. i also happened to come across the book after overhearing a whole-ass debate about whether a man should be the head of the family and lead in every aspect, while a woman should simply listen and follow.

i have never really liked the saying, “Behind every successful man is a supportive woman.” i much prefer the idea of “Beside every successful man is a successful woman.” i value equality in a relationship, so i was hoping this book would not lean too far into the whole far-right, “men do not cry” school of thought.

i was pleasantly surprised by how Matt Fuller presents his points and navigates the nuances of modern gender dynamics alongside Scripture. For me, the central takeaway was the importance of striving to be a godly man who seeks Christ, and thinking about what that looks like in everyday life.

i particularly enjoyed his exploration of servant leadership, including protecting and caring for your family and congregation, and being a guiding light for younger men. His discussions gave me plenty to reflect on about faith, masculinity and the responsibilities that come with leadership.

Overall, i would recommend this book to anyone interested in exploring the relationship between contemporary gender politics and Christianity, especially younger men trying to make sense of it all. And please, stop consuming the toxic masculinity crap that people like Andrew Tate put out.

My rating: 4/5.
